A similar experiment was carried out with an albino tobacco leaf (lower panel) which do not photosynthesize. Shaded portions denote ${ }^{14} \mathrm{C}$ labelling.


Based on these observations the correct option(s) is(are)
options: In the early stages of development, the leaf acts as a source.
Mature leaf gains the ability to load and export sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
The process of opening and closing of stomata (called stomatal movement) is controlled by turgor pressure changes in the guard cells. A list of events is given below.
(i) Water potential becomes less negative
(ii) Guard cells shrink
(iii) Water potential becomes more negative
(iv) Guard cells swell
(v) $\mathrmK^{+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ diffuse passively out of the cell
(vi) Water is taken up by the cells
(vii) Water diffuses out of the cell by osmosis
(viii) Stomata close
(ix) Stomata open
(x) $\mathrmK^{+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ actively move into the cell The correct sequence of events occurring in the guard cells leading to stomatal movement during a period of darkness in most plants would be:
options: (v) \rightarrow (i) \rightarrow (vii) \rightarrow (ii) \rightarrow (viii)
(x) \rightarrow (iii) \rightarrow (vi) \rightarrow (iv) \rightarrow (ix)
(v) \rightarrow (iii) \rightarrow (vi) \rightarrow (iv) \rightarrow (ix)
(x) \rightarrow (i) \rightarrow (vii) \rightarrow (ii) \rightarrow (viii)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
The ability of phloem to distribute sugar depends on the companion cell and sieve element working as a complex. Consider the following statements with regard to possible effects of reduction in companion cell plasmodesmata.
(i) Sugar loading into sieve tubes reduces due to collapse in osmotic pressure gradient.
(ii) Water moves from companion cells into the xylem to maintain osmotic balance.
(iii) The sieve tubes collapse structurally due to loss of turgor pressure.
(iv) Reverse loading of sugar in phloem begins immediately due to pressure inversion.
Under the given condition, the correct statements are:
options: (iii) and (iv)
(i) and (iii)
(i) and (ii)
(ii) and (iv)
questions.solution:
Companion cells and sieve tube elements function together as a complex to load and transport sugars in the phloem. Sugars are loaded from companion cells into sieve tubes through plasmodesmata.

If there is a reduction in companion cell plasmodesmata, the transfer of sugars into the sieve tubes is hindered. This leads to a significant decrease in sugar loading, which in turn causes a collapse in the osmotic pressure gradient that normally draws water into the phloem.

Due to the reduced solute concentration in the sieve tubes, less water enters from the adjacent xylem. This results in a severe drop in turgor pressure within the sieve tubes, which can cause them to structurally collapse.

Statements (ii) and (iv) are incorrect as water does not move from companion cells to xylem to maintain balance, and reverse loading due to pressure inversion does not occur. Thus, statements (i) and (iii) correctly describe the physiological consequences.

Answer: (i) and (iii)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A leaf-infecting fungus secretes a chemical that causes the guard cells to remain open thereby enabling the fungus to enter the plant tissue through the stomata. The most likely function of this chemical is
options: importing sodium ions into the guard cells.
exporting potassium ions out of the guard cells.
exporting water molecules out of the guard cells.
importing potassium ions into the guard cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which one of the following occurs during osmosis?
options: The movement of water from a concentrated solution to a dilute solution across a semi-permeable membrane.
The movement of a dissolved substance from a concentrated solution to a dilute solution across a semi-permeable membrane.
The movement of water from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution across a semi-permeable membrane.
The movement of a solute from a dilute solution across a semi-permeable membrane.
